title: feat(connector-openapi): normalize-openapi --trim writes only the operations --include-pattern matches
body:
Fixes #28309
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:离线脚本 `normalize-openapi` 新增 `--trim` 开关,配合 `--include-pattern` 只写出被匹配的操作;两处文档同步。
- 为什么改:大型厂商文档(Stripe 612 个操作、63 MB)原样打包不现实;Stripe 连接器应用要求打包文件就是脚本输出并记录其 sha256。
- 风险与回滚:只改仓库脚本(不随 npm 发布)与文档;不加 `--trim` 时输出逐字节不变;回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/connectors/connector-openapi/scripts/normalize-openapi.mts` 的 `trimPaths` 与第 4 步前的裁剪调用;其测试文件的 `--trim` 一节;`content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx` 新段落。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/connector-openapi exec vitest run scripts/normalize-openapi.test.ts`,预期 20 个测试全部通过。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

- `scripts/normalize-openapi.mts` gains `--trim` (option `trim` on `normalizeOpenApi`). With it, every path operation no `--include-pattern` matches, every path item left with no operation, and `webhooks` are dropped **before** dereferencing, so only the kept operations are walked and nothing reachable only from a dropped operation reaches the output. A `$ref` path item is resolved (not walked) before its operations are selected. The `include` list is computed exactly as before (same patterns, same imported `operationActionKey`), and the printed `sha256` is still the hash of the bytes written, which are now the trimmed bytes. The summary gains `trimmedFrom` (operations in the source) when trimming. `--trim` with no `--include-pattern` is refused (exit 1); a pattern matching nothing is refused as before.
- `securitySchemes` stay, as in the untrimmed path (they are referenced by name, never by `$ref`, and the provider does not read them); every other component was already dropped after inlining, and under `--trim` it is never reached from a dropped operation.
- Docs: `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx` (the script's paragraph: the example command now carries `--trim`, and a new paragraph says what trimming writes and when to leave it off); `content/docs/deployment/marketplace-handbook.mdx`, the one README-section sentence that still described the normalizer as forthcoming now says how a declarative OpenAPI app produces its packaged document and which sha256 to record.
- The runtime (`src/**`) does not change; the script stays a repository script (not in `files[]`, no `bin`), so this carries `skip-changeset`.

### Why a separate `--trim` flag, not trimming whenever `--include-pattern` is given

- An implied trim changes what the one documented command writes (its bytes and its hash) with no change to the command line. With a flag, every existing invocation writes exactly what it wrote before: the untrimmed Stripe run below reproduces the #28276 reading byte for byte.
- The two outputs serve two different authors. Untrimmed plus `include` lets an app widen `include` later by editing config alone; trimmed means widening requires re-running the script. Which one an app wants is the author's call, and the command line that produced the packaged bytes should say which one it was.
- Today's callers: the only documented call is the example in `connectors.mdx` (the shelf pipeline is not built yet), so the flag costs nobody a migration; the example now uses `--trim`, which is what recipe 1 teaches (trim to the operations the app calls).

## Tests

`scripts/normalize-openapi.test.ts`, on the existing fixtures, a new `--trim` block and one new CLI case:

- the trimmed output holds exactly the matched operations (`GetCustomers`, `GetCustomersCustomer`, `get_v1_balance`), drops the unmatched POST from a path item whose GET is kept, has the same `include` list as the untrimmed run, loads through `createOpenApiProviderFactory` with exactly those actions and no `$ref` in the document or the materialized def;
- trimming to `balance` alone drops the customer path items and leaves no text reachable only from them (`A customer.`, `Error response.`, the shared `limit` parameter, `subscription`), with zero cuts counted (only the kept operation was walked);
- a Swagger 2.0 document is trimmed after conversion, keyed by `operationId`;
- a `$ref` path item is resolved before selection (its sibling `summary` kept) and `webhooks` are dropped;
- refusals: `--trim` with no pattern; a pattern matching nothing;
- control: without `--trim` the whole document is written, as before;
- CLI: with `--trim`, `bytes` and `sha256` equal the written file's length and `sha256` of its bytes, `operations` is 2 and `trimmedFrom` is 4; `--trim` alone exits 1 and writes nothing.

## Acceptance notes

Measured once against the real Stripe document, `stripe/openapi` `openapi/spec3.json` at `51610f5f` (MIT; 8,317,513 bytes, sha256 `7cff4cc46d0654101a36a3302f7544640f5f73e4f3cad6f264f0e23c19fa1776`), with the pattern `^(GetCustomers|PostCustomers|GetCustomersCustomer|GetCharges|PostPaymentIntents|GetPaymentIntentsIntent)$` at the default `--max-depth 2`:

| run | bytes | operations | sha256 |
|:---|---:|---:|:---|
| without `--trim` (control) | 63,317,655 | 612 | `0ea3c37a0854ad2646a156404b1ef86cca57403855e3803cd4630601eb6fc7b2` |
| with `--trim` | 1,934,435 | 6 (`trimmedFrom` 612) | `08d6e40bccec707a0bfc355b1cbf936df29018c22e7be658d616683e501b13d4` |

- The control equals the #28276 dev's reading byte for byte (same size, same hash), so the untrimmed path is unchanged on the real document.
- `sha256sum` of the trimmed file equals the printed hash; `refsLeft` 0; cuts recursive 38, max-depth 1064, extension 240; the two runs print the same `include` list.
- The trimmed file loads through `createOpenApiProviderFactory` with exactly the six actions and zero `$ref` keys in the text and in the materialized def.
- The trimmed size is about 1.9 MB, not the about 1.1 MB the card quoted: the #28276 dev's six operations are not named on that card, so this is a different six (two of them creates carrying request bodies). The number is a reading of this pattern, not a target.
